title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Criminals are using generative AI to create convincing impersonations, cloning the voices and identities of real people, including a South Florida immigration attorney, to deceive victims on social media and over the phone. The system failure here is one of platform governance: social media platforms lack sufficient controls to prevent fraudsters from using deepfakes and voice cloning to impersonate real professionals and build false credibility with vulnerable populations like immigrants seeking legal services.

This is impersonation enabled by AI generation tools deployed without verification. Victims lost money because they could not distinguish between real professionals and AI-generated copies. The fraud could have been caught or prevented by platforms requiring identity verification for accounts offering legal services, by monitoring for suspicious use of generative AI tools to clone public figures, or by educating users about verification methods before sending money.

It is not established whether the platforms hosting these scams were aware of the impersonations, whether the generative AI tools were deployed by their makers with safeguards against this use, or whether any specific companies bear responsibility for these particular frauds.

summary:
Criminals are increasingly using artificial intelligence to commit sophisticated scams across Georgia and South Florida. The FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report found that Americans lost nearly $893 million to AI-enabled scams last year. Specific cases included a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice and identity were cloned to target immigrants, and a Cobb County couple who lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam. Florida reported 350 AI-related complaints with nearly $39.9 million in losses, while Georgia had 71 complaints resulting in more than $10.4 million in losses. The FBI received over 1 million internet crime complaints overall totaling more than $20 billion in reported losses.

Scammers are using generative AI to make traditional fraud schemes far more convincing by cloning voices from social media, spoofing phone numbers, creating fake photographs, and researching personal relationships. Common scams include the grandparent scheme where criminals mimic relatives' voices to request emergency money, romance scams that resulted in over $19 million in losses, and distress calls involving voice cloning. Authorities recommend families create private code words to verify identities, verify urgent requests through known phone numbers, avoid sending money based on phone calls alone, and report suspected scams to law enforcement immediately.
